payout_quote: Each Vote Center is staffed by 8-12 Election Officers and currently the rate of pay is: $20 per hour to serve 4 days at a Vote Center. Additional stipend of $60 for attending a mandatory training session. Election Day begins at 6:00 a.m. and ends at approximately 10:00 p.m.
steps: Be a California resident, 18 years old on or before Election Day (students 16+ have additional requirements).
Apply to be an Election Officer via the Registrar of Voters (voteinfo.net).
Attend the mandatory training session (pays a $60 stipend, separate from Election Day pay).
Serve Election Day at a vote center, 6:00 a.m. to approximately 10:00 p.m. (the county's vote-center model also uses officers for 4 days total; this route is framed on Election Day only).
catches: Framed on Election Day only ($320 for 6:00 a.m.-~10:00 p.m.); the county's vote-center model also staffs officers across 4 days, which would pay more at $20/hr but with unstated daily hours.
Mandatory training pays a separate $60 stipend and is excluded from this Election-Day payout and time.
Long day: Election Day runs 6:00 a.m. to approximately 10:00 p.m.
Must be a California resident and able to read and write English.
Pay timing not stated on the official page.
biggest_catch: $320 covers Election Day only (6 a.m. to ~10 p.m.); the mandatory $60 training stipend and any additional vote-center days are separate and not included.
eligibility: California resident, 18+ on Election Day (students 16+ with additional requirements), able to read and write English.
timing: Pay timing not stated on the official page.
